units.translation: For thus Stanley corrected what is read in M as les τὴν καταφθατουμένην [the one being overtaken], although with the nominative gloss καταφθάνουσα [overtaking] written in the margin. Hesychius: καταφθατουμένη [being overtaken]: καταντωμένη [being met] (κατακτωμένη [being acquired] in the codex) · properly, that which comes from anticipation. It is not found elsewhere.
From afar I heard the voice of a report from Scamander, overtaking the land.
properly, that which comes from anticipation
Much wealth has been utterly destroyed.
Around Athens the whole army has been utterly destroyed.
The whole people has been utterly destroyed by the spear.

You, having destroyed the ancient allotment (thus I corrected what is in M as 1η παλαιάς δαίμονας, in the scholium on Eur. Alc. 12 written παλαιὰς διανομάς [ancient distributions]) with wine, deceived the ancient goddesses.
But when the light of the sun had perished.
Aeschylus – this monument hides him, perished, from wheat-bearing Gela.
Thus I wrote for κατεψέκαζον [they were sprinkling]. For the Attics said ψακάς [a drop] and ψακάζω [I drip], not ψεκάς and ψεκάζω: see Thes. vol. 8 p. 1828.
to return, the present indicative having the meaning of the future 'I will return'
A wandering exile, a stranger to this land, will return.
Aorist subjunctive κατειργαθεῖν, whose middle form is κατειργαθέσθαι
Thus rightly Porson, except that he wrote κατειργάθου [you were confined] with a false accent. κατεργάθου in M.
Proclaim, herald, and confine the army.
You were slain by the spear.
The mattock of Zeus, with which the ground has been worked.
Tearing their veils with soft hands.
When you returned to the city.
Having returned here with favorable fortune.
For I have come to this land and am returning.
And I, having returned, after fleeing for a time before, killed the woman who bore me.
For the curses of Oedipus boiled over.
I praise the words of these prayers.
And to what end do I meet with prayers?
With dative, to pour out prayers to someone
What fortunes she prays for and curses!
What I pray for – to draw up from the earth the bright light of the sun, fortunes of life that are beneficial and swift.
How shall I pray to my father?
I pray to you that Orestes may come here with some fortune.
Hear, blessed ones of the underworld, this prayer.
To dwell in the land, having divided as much as to hold even for the dead.
